modern: If any man is able to convince me and show me that I do not think or act rightly, I will gladly change; for I seek the truth, by which no man was ever harmed. But he is harmed who persists in his error and ignorance.
original: If any man is able to convince me and show me that I do not think or act right, I will gladly change; for I seek the truth, by which no man was ever injured. But he is injured who abides in his error and ignorance.

notification_original: If any man is able to convince me and show me that I do not think or act right, I will gladly change; for I seek the truth, by which no man was ever injured.

explained.summary: If someone can show Marcus he’s thinking or acting wrongly, he’ll gladly change. He’s after the truth, and the truth never harmed anyone. What harms you is clinging to a mistake out of pride or ignorance. Being corrected is a gift, not a defeat.
explained.today: When someone points out an error in your spreadsheet, or a friend says you were unfair in an argument, the instinct is to defend yourself. Saying ’you’re right, thanks’ costs a moment’s pride and leaves you better off.
